title: QUESTION: concurrent branches - grants and revocations racing a demotion/revocation
description: From vouch-ey47.13 review. Order is now ancestry (git-vouch History.before), since topo order of merged branches is author-controlled. Implemented (Claude, for Mark's review): (a) a tier record added on a branch concurrent with a commit that lowered its approver's authority is an error (conservative; a real grant made on a long-lived branch while the approver was demoted on main must be re-approved). (b) A revocation signed by a key that is revoked in a concurrent (not ancestor) commit still counts, extending 'revocations in one commit all count'; the other choice can leave a stolen key unrevoked when owner and thief revoke each other on concurrent branches. Risk of (b): a compromised anchor key can still revoke keys from a branch forked before its own revocation, and committed revocations cannot be undone. Owner's call on both.
